high.title: This Brazilian Stock Can Benefit Even From a 'Worst Case Scenario' for the Selic Rate, According to Analyst
high.summary: The Selic rate cutting cycle, widely expected for 2026, began at the last COPOM meeting on March 18th, but the magnitude of cuts may fall short of initial market expectations. By mid-February, most of the market was pricing in a terminal Selic rate of 12% per year in 2026. However, the Middle East war has brought greater inflationary pressure, deteriorating expectations. According to Empiricus Research analyst Ruy Hungria, "If we started the year expecting to see Selic at 12% at the end of 2026, now that number has been revised to 13.5%-13.75%, and could rise further depending on the conflict's extension." This deterioration in interest rate outlook typically scares equity investors, as highly leveraged companies face direct impact from high rates on their debt. The article suggests there's a specific Brazilian stock that could benefit even from this adverse scenario, though the details of which stock are not provided in this excerpt.

high.title: Markets Rise Optimistic With Peace Negotiations; Oil Falls and Ibovespa in Dollars Rises Today (14)
high.summary: Global markets advanced on Tuesday (14th) while oil prices declined, reflecting relief signals in Middle East geopolitical tensions. The movement gained momentum after US President Donald Trump indicated openness to resume negotiations with Iran, reinforcing expectations of a more consistent ceasefire in the region. According to Bloomberg sources, Washington and Tehran are discussing the possibility of new negotiation rounds to extend the two-week truce established on April 7th, whose deadline expires in the coming days. The intention is to advance an agreement before the end of this period, amid intensifying diplomatic efforts. Despite the more conciliatory discourse, the US maintains pressure strategy on Iran, having initiated a naval blockade limiting vessel entry and exit from Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. This geopolitical development is crucial for BRL traders as reduced tensions typically support risk assets and could influence BCB policy decisions.

high.title: Oil Rises Despite Expectations of Resumed US-Iran Negotiations
high.summary: After a period of decline on Wednesday (15th), oil prices rose despite expectations that peace negotiations between the US and Iran could be resumed and that supply could eventually return to the market from the main Middle Eastern producing region affected by the Strait of Hormuz closure. Brent futures were up 85 cents, or 0.90%, to $95.64 per barrel at 5:50 AM (Brasília time), after a 4.6% decline in the previous session. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 42 cents, or 0.46%, to $91.70, after falling 7.9% in the previous session. The war has practically interrupted traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial maritime route for transporting crude oil and derivatives from the Gulf to global buyers, especially in Asia and Europe. President Trump stated that negotiations with Tehran to end the war could resume this week. This oil price volatility directly impacts Brazil through Petrobras and inflation expectations, influencing BCB monetary policy decisions.

medium.title: Ibovespa at 196,000 Points: 'It Won't Take Much Effort to Reach 200,000 Points', Says Analyst; See 10 Stocks to Buy Now
medium.summary: For the third consecutive session, the Ibovespa continues to defy the macroeconomic scenario and hit new highs, touching 197,554 points on Friday (10th). The index has gained 4% this week despite an unstable environment for risk assets. IBGE released March IPCA data showing 0.88% acceleration, above market projections of 0.77%. Empiricus Research analyst Ruy Hungria views the index's resilience amid turbulence as a clear signal that reaching 200,000 points won't require much effort.

medium.title: Vale (VALE3) Shares Can Unlock More Value Thanks to Little-Known 'Crown Jewel', According to Analyst
medium.summary: Vale (VALE3) closed March down 6.77% but still accumulates a 14.6% gain in 2026, after rising 49% in 2025. Empiricus Research analyst Ruy Hungria views the decline as profit-taking given iron ore price resilience and possible commodity rotation toward oil. The analyst believes Vale has an undernoticed "crown jewel" that could drive shares to attractive levels, with the company showing relevant operational evolution and benefiting from dollar revenues amid uncertainty.

medium.title: Real Time: Ibovespa Follows More China Data and Retail Sales in Brazil
medium.summary: The Ibovespa tracks a battery of China data: GDP, industrial production, retail sales and unemployment rate. Domestically, retail sales numbers and IGP-10 are released, while in the US the Federal Reserve's Beige Book comes out. Stone (STNE) announced an extraordinary dividend payment of approximately R$ 3.1 billion in May, equivalent to R$ 2.53 per share.
